Source [S1] supports the bilinear interpolation, normalization to [0, 1], and saving as PNG slices. Source [S2] supports the normalization to [0, 1] and saving as a raw uint16 file. However, the claim implies a single method performs all these actions or that the evidence supports the combination of these specific options within one described workflow. While the individual facts (bilinear resize, PNG save, raw uint16 save, normalization) are present in the evidence across the two sources, the claim presents them as a unified set of capabilities ('This method...'). More critically, Source [S1] mentions rotating 90 degrees, which is not in the claim, but that doesn't make it unsupported. The main issue is that the claim combines features from two different sources/methods into one description. However, looking strictly at 'every fact in it is in the evidence': 1. Resizes using bilinear interpolation (S1). 2. Normalizes to [0,1] (S1, S2). 3. Saves as PNG slices (S1). 4. Saves as raw uint16 (S2). All specific factual components are present in the provided evidence. The 'optionally' suggests these are alternative outputs. Since both outputs are described in the evidence, the claim is supported by the aggregate evidence.
